ca_stirrup_tank.blurb: Stirrup Tank is a quiet pocket of Joshua Tree National Park in the Pinto Basin, well away from the busier western side of the park. Most of the climbing is traditional, with a fair amount of sport and some top-rope routes, and the grades run from very easy up through a big middle of moderates and 5.10s, with a handful of low 5.12s at the top. Rock quality is uneven, from poor to good, and much of the stone has a smooth, polished feel. Stirrup Rock, a brown granite crag, gives you a seasonal choice: its south face is a sheltered sun trap in winter, while the north face stays shaded in warmer months. Zippy Rock and Stirrup Towers are the other larger crags.

co_eldorado_mountain.blurb: Eldorado Mountain stands just south of Eldorado Canyon on the eastern edge of Colorado's Front Range, outside Boulder. The climbing is scattered across numbered ridges, towers and walls above a talus field, so expect some walking between crags. Bolted sport routes outnumber trad roughly two to one, and the grades build from moderate to a strong middle of 5.10 through 5.12, with a few 5.13s and the odd 5.14. On Ridge 4 the crags are short, face south, and are sandstone with plenty of edges, flakes and corners. Mickey Mouse Wall holds the most routes and is mainly trad, while Ridge 1 and the Industrial Wall lean toward sport.

_expect.name: Boulders Behind the Main Parking Lot/Visitor Center

vt_boulders_behind_the_main_parking_lot_.blurb: This is the biggest cluster of bouldering in Smugglers' Notch, the mountain gap between Mount Mansfield and Spruce Peak near Stowe in northern Vermont. The blocks sit on the Mansfield side of the Notch in a dense maze of caves and passages that is easy to get turned around in, and it packs more quality problems into one spot than anywhere else in the Notch. Everything here is bouldering, from V0 up past V12, with a healthy number of problems at every level, from tall highballs to short, core-heavy ones. Many problems dry quickly thanks to the elevation and exposure. Green Cave is the largest single area, followed by Biscuit and Gravy Boulders and the Brewski Boulder.

wa_snoqualmie_pass_area.blurb: Snoqualmie Pass Area, in Washington's Central-West Cascades near Seattle, offers nearly every kind of climbing: sport and trad crags, alpine peaks, ice, scrambling and a little bouldering. The year splits by season. Ice, snow and mixed routes dominate winter and spring, with ice from WI2 to WI6, while rock climbing takes over in summer and fall at places like The Tooth, Chair Peak and Keechelus Ridge. Crag grades are mostly 5.7 to 5.11, and the scrambles run from class 2 to 4. Keechelus Ridge is blocky andesite that faces southeast, so it can bake in July. Exit 47 is rounded, fine-grained granite in small, mostly shady outcrops, handy for top-roping, with some freeway noise.

wi_south_bluff.blurb: South Bluff is a large, mesa-like ridge south of Devil's Lake in Wisconsin's Baraboo Range, crowned by ledges and boulders of quartzite. Nearly all of the bouldering sits near the rim, and the north rim looks out over the lake. The problems run from very easy to V10, with the most volume between V0 and V3 and a solid group of harder ones above V6. It feels remote for the Midwest: there are no official trails, a few easy user paths lead to The Reserve, the largest sub-area, and other zones such as Surprise and Ghost Talus take bushwhacking or boulder-hopping to reach. You will likely have the place to yourself.

wy_devils_tower.blurb: Devils Tower is a huge, isolated column of phonolite porphyry that rises above grassland and ponderosa pine forest in Wyoming, with a boulder field of broken columns at its base. Parallel cracks split the rock into big hexagonal columns, and the climbing follows them: mostly traditional crack routes, from hand-width to body-width, long and sustained. Routes are mostly 5.9 to 5.12, with a few easier ones, a handful of bolted face climbs, some aid and a few boulder problems. The West Face has the most routes, followed by the South and East Faces. The rock can get very hot in summer, and storms build quickly.
